title: Loop the Loopies!
hook: Looping a Transformer instead of growing it usually loses to just adding more parameters — Loopie is the looped MoE model that finally breaks that pattern, with IMO/IPhO gold-level reasoning.
key_points: Loopie: two looped-Transformer MoE models — 20B params (2B active) and 6B params (0.6B active).
Long-standing problem: for an N-fold compute increase, growing parameters by N usually beats looping N times — Loopie is built to close that gap.
Beats vanilla Transformer baselines trained at the same compute budget, including a vanilla 30B-A3B comparison.
A novel post-training pipeline gives Loopie strong reasoning abilities on top of the looped-MoE backbone.
Achieves gold-medal-level performance on 2025 IMO and IPhO problems without using external tools.
content_html: Looped Transformers — reusing the same layers multiple times instead of stacking new ones — have long promised compute efficiency, but kept losing to the simpler trick of just adding more parameters. Loopie is the authors' attempt to finally make looping pay off.
extra_html:
Zitian Gao, Bryan Dai, and colleagues present Loopie, described as the most powerful looped Transformer to date, released as two Mixture-of-Experts models: 20B total parameters with 2B active, and 6B total with 0.6B active. Through extensive ablations — including a head-to-head with a vanilla 30B-A3B baseline — they show Loopie substantially outperforms standard Transformer baselines trained under the same compute budget, addressing the well-known gap where looping N times usually loses to scaling parameters by N.

A novel post-training pipeline then equips Loopie with strong reasoning ability: the model reaches gold-medal-level performance on the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad and International Physics Olympiad problem sets, without relying on external tools. Paper posted to arXiv, July 2026.

related.title: Switch Transformer: Scaling to Trillion-Parameter Models
related.hook: Route every token to exactly one expert instead of many - this single simplification made trillion-parameter MoE models stable enough to train at scale.

related.title: Mixtral of Experts
related.hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.

flashcards.prompt: What long-standing tradeoff has made looped Transformers a hard sell?
flashcards.back_html: Given an N-fold increase in compute, simply multiplying parameter count by N usually beats looping the same model N times — looping tended to underperform scaling up.
